text: Technology theme should be treated as an AI/cloud infrastructure buildout that pulls on physical semiconductor capacity, advanced packaging, optical connectivity, power/cooling infrastructure, cybersecurity and automation rather than as a single mega-cap software or GPU theme.

Semiconductor equipment subsystem suppliers remain the highest-conviction underfollowed lane because they sit below visible equipment OEMs and can benefit from qualification lock-in across vacuum, power delivery, gas/chemical delivery, process control and contamination-control subsystems.
Advanced packaging substrate materials and capacity, especially ABF/build-up film and high-end substrate suppliers, should be tracked as a core AI accelerator bottleneck lane.
AI optical connectivity should be mapped below transceiver assemblers into lasers, silicon photonics, compound-semiconductor wafers, epitaxy capacity and epitaxy tools.
High-purity quartz remains a systemic but difficult-to-express public-market shadow bottleneck; public candidates should be treated cautiously unless direct revenue or dependency evidence is found.

Cybersecurity, automation and data-center power/cooling candidates need primary-source validation before they can be ranked with the same confidence as semiconductor subsystem and packaging-material candidates.
Layer 2 should verify market-cap buckets, analyst coverage, revenue purity, customer concentration, qualification cycles, capacity constraints, and recent pricing/crowding for all candidates.

For the Technology theme, current evidence points to AI infrastructure as the active branch; map demand from AI accelerators into physical bottlenecks rather than stopping at mega-cap chip/platform names.
High-end IC package substrates are a priority bottleneck node because Ibiden announced large AI/high-performance-server substrate capex with mass production planned from fiscal 2027.

ABF build-up film should be treated as an upstream substrate-material gate; evidence confirms ABF is used in high-performance semiconductor package substrates, but current allocation tightness needs further verification.
AI-server MLCCs and power modules are emerging second-order bottleneck nodes; Murata explicitly cited increased server capacitors and power-supply modules in its April 30, 2026 forecast.
Data-center electrical distribution and behind-the-meter power should be tracked as physical deployment bottlenecks; Powell's fiscal Q2 2026 results provide order and backlog evidence.

Semiconductor equipment subsystems, contamination control, specialty chemistry, and cleaning services remain underfollowed nodes that may capture value from advanced-node and advanced-packaging capacity expansion.
Compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools are a hypothesis node tied to AI optical connectivity; verify through order intake, customer commentary, and laser/InP/GaAs capacity signals.

Track future catalysts: substrate capex announcements, customer prepayments, MLCC price/lead-time commentary, power-equipment backlog, data-center grid/permitting policy, and qualification wins at underfollowed suppliers.
Need direct primary evidence on ABF supply tightness, current market share, customer allocation terms, and whether substrate makers have secured enough film for planned AI-server capacity.

Need source-backed checks for low-attention distributors, certification labs, test-socket suppliers, high-speed connector suppliers, cold-plate/CDU vendors, and electrical contractors before candidate ranking.

Need to separate facts from market narratives in Substack-style sources by validating claims against filings, earnings calls, investor presentations, customer disclosures, and regulator or permitting records.
For this Technology candidate chunk, the main mapped chokepoint families are semicap embedded subsystems and advanced packaging substrate/material capacity, not headline AI chip designers.

Ibiden has the strongest primary evidence in the chunk because its February 3, 2026 release directly links a large fiscal 2026-2028 capex plan to high-performance IC package substrates for AI and high-performance servers.

Ajinomoto has strong node evidence as an ABF build-up film supplier to high-performance package substrate manufacturers, but current market share, capacity allocation, customer mix, and substitute qualification remain open checks.

MKS, Ichor, Ultra Clean, and Advanced Energy require primary-source refresh for latest semiconductor revenue mix, customer concentration, book-to-bill, cleanroom utilization, and explicit advanced-node or advanced-packaging exposure.

Aixtron's AI relationship should remain a hypothesis until application-level orders show optical, laser, InP, GaAs, or other AI data-center connectivity pull-through rather than primarily power electronics or microLED cyclicality.

Unimicron and AT&S need ticker normalization, current market-cap verification, substrate revenue split, AI/HPC customer proof, ABF access, utilization, capex timing, and balance-sheet checks before surviving to later Serenity layers.

COHU mapped to semiconductor test handlers, interface products, and services as an underfollowed second-order AI/advanced-packaging test-intensity hypothesis; primary evidence needed from filings and earnings calls.
FORM mapped to probe cards and wafer-level test interfaces as an underfollowed HBM/AI accelerator test chokepoint hypothesis; verify HBM, logic, and customer concentration exposure.
TSEM mapped to silicon-photonics specialty foundry capacity as an underfollowed AI optical-connectivity hypothesis; materiality to revenue remains unverified.
CRDO mapped to high-speed connectivity, SerDes, active electrical cables, and signal integrity for AI cluster networking; verify customer concentration and AEC/socket-win durability.

LITE, COHR, FN, MTSI, and SMTC map into the optical connectivity stack, but the next layer must separate module manufacturing, lasers, optical components, signal-integrity chips, and specialty foundry capacity to avoid overgeneralizing AI optical exposure.

Most ticker relationships in this chunk are still based on candidate-map hypotheses or cached Layer 1 classifications rather than primary filings. Layer 2C should collect current 10-K/10-Q/annual report and earnings-call evidence for AI, HBM, advanced packaging, 800G/1.6T, data center, and customer-concentration language.

Market-pricing checks were not performed in this Layer 2B call. Later layers should verify current market caps, valuation dispersion, analyst coverage, short interest, recent price reaction, and whether any candidate remains genuinely underfollowed.
Semtech's candidate entry is truncated in the provided chunk; treat SMTC as speculative_shadow until the full candidate note and primary evidence are retrieved.

POWL should be promoted within this chunk from hypothesis toward evidence-supported underfollowed relationship because primary-source evidence shows fiscal Q2 2026 new orders of about $490 million, backlog of about $1.8 billion, and a post-quarter data-center order exceeding $400 million tied to behind-the-meter on-site generation assets.

MOD remains a potentially important AI data-center cooling candidate, but its relationship should stay hypothesis-level until filings or transcripts verify data-center revenue share, liquid-cooling product exposure, backlog, capacity, and customer evidence.

NVT maps to data-center enclosures, connections, thermal, and electrical infrastructure as an underfollowed industrial-electrical name, but requires company-level validation of data-center mix and AI-related order pull.

STRL maps to data-center site infrastructure and e-infrastructure construction, but the relationship is indirect and requires backlog/customer evidence to distinguish hyperscale AI exposure from ordinary infrastructure construction.
BELFA should remain speculative_shadow until product-level and customer-level evidence confirms AI-networking or data-center power-component revenue rather than broad electronics exposure.

VICR maps to AI power-delivery and high-density power-conversion nodes, but survival in later layers depends on evidence of current design wins, customer concentration, revenue ramp, and IP/litigation status.

VRNS, TENB, and S represent software/security demand-side AI beneficiaries rather than physical chokepoints; later layers should test whether AI/cloud complexity is producing measurable ARR acceleration, retention strength, or customer expansion.
IOT is an indirect AI/automation data-layer candidate; later evidence must show AI feature monetization, enterprise expansion, and durable retention rather than general fleet/IoT SaaS growth only.

For MOD, NVT, STRL, BELFA, VICR, VRNS, TENB, S, and IOT, no supplied primary-source evidence yet confirms AI-specific revenue share or customer demand; these names should not be ranked as validated chokepoints until latest filings, earnings transcripts, and product disclosures are checked.

Market-pricing checks remain incomplete for all tickers in this chunk; later layers should quantify market cap, recent price reaction, valuation multiples, analyst coverage, ownership concentration, and crowding without converting the output into buy/sell recommendations.
